    Synopsis:
        Unusually high jellyfish concentrations are impacting Delaware beaches in summer 2024, driven by warmer waters, drought-elevated salinity, favorable wind/circulation patterns, and a quiet hurricane season. Sting rates of 100–200/day are deterring swimmers. Four species are flagged. Scientists warn conditions may worsen long-term. A parallel stingray surge is noted in southern California.
